_README: The tracker (_migrations_applied) is keyed by FILENAME. A migration that was applied and then
renumbered looks brand-new under its new name and would be RE-APPLIED. The runner refuses to
guess; an operator records the answer here.
This file is EMPTY BY DESIGN. It is not a backlog — an entry is only ever added at the moment a
real renumber blocks a real deploy, and it pins ONE specific (new_filename, applied_filename,
sql_identity) triple. If any of the three changes, the guard fails loudly again. Every field is
required; a partial entry is dropped and treated as UNDISCLOSED, never as a partial pass (same
disposition must be exactly one of:
already-applied-under-old-name — the SQL genuinely ran under applied_filename. The runner
records new_filename as applied WITHOUT executing it. This is the normal answer.
intentional-reapply — the SQL is idempotent and re-running it under the new name is the
deliberate intent. The runner executes it normally.
cd platform && npx tsx -e "import {sqlIdentityOf} from './scripts/migrate.ts'; import fs from 'fs'; console.log(sqlIdentityOf(fs.readFileSync(process.argv[1],'utf8')))" <path-to-sql>
Two historical instances of this hazard are recorded (as history, not as entries) in

entries.reason: bg_parihara_rules was initially filed as 485_bg_parihara_rules.sql and applied to production. During the ṢAḌ-DARŚANA campaign it was renumbered to 544 to reflect its actual dependency order relative to migrations 486–543. The SQL content is identical (only the -- Migration NNN: header comment differs, which is stripped by sqlIdentityOf). Production already has this table; the runner should record 544 as applied without re-executing.
